The *Sāriputta Sutta* (Ud 3.4; PTS Ud 27) is a short canonical discourse located in the third chapter of the Pali *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. The text portrays the Venerable Sāriputta in meditation, his mind steady and firm as a rock [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records sixteen translations of the discourse across thirteen languages, including an English rendering by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. None of the reference literature passages supplied in the dossier concern this specific *Udāna* discourse; all homonymous citations refer instead to the *Sāriputta Sutta* of the *Sutta Nipāta* (Sn 4.16), discourses in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, or teachings of Sāriputta in the *Majjhima* and *Dīgha Nikāyas*.

SuttaCentral notes verse-level parallels to the discourse in several other Buddhist traditions, including the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* recensions (UV 32 and UVS 32, *Bhikṣuvarga*; Uv Kg 32), two Chinese versions of the *Udānavarga* / *Udāna* (T 212.33 and T 213.32), as well as two poems in the Pali *Theragāthā* (Thag 17.2, *Sāriputtattheragāthā*, and Thag 14.1, *Khadiravaniyarevatattheragāthā*) [SuttaCentral]. While DharmaNexus reports no cross-language matches meeting its threshold, its automated analysis identifies 25 Pali-internal reuse passages across ten texts [DharmaNexus]. These matches reflect shared stock narrative formulas and contemplative descriptions found in other *Udāna* suttas—most extensively with the *Kaṅkhārevata Sutta* (Ud 5.7, sharing §1.1–3.1 with §1.1–4.1), the *Taṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (Ud 7.6, sharing §0.2–3.1 with §0.2–4.1), the *Sāriputtaupasama Sutta* (Ud 4.10), the adjacent *Mahāmoggallāna Sutta* (Ud 3.5), the *Cūḷapanthaka Sutta* (Ud 5.10), the *Subhūti Sutta* (Ud 6.7), another *Sāriputta Sutta* (Ud 4.7), and the *Kaccāna Sutta* (Ud 7.8)—as well as the *Bāhiya Sutta* (Ud 1.10) and the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1, sharing §1.3–1.4 with §15.3.1–15.3.2) [DharmaNexus].
